title: Hold the hunt return's multipart body to its cap as it is read
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/audio/hunt-return/route.ts buffers a chunked (no content-length) body whole: the same defect 27aa7ffb fixed in /audio/return.

## Description
hunt-return/route.ts:33 passes `bodyCap: MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1_000_000` to route(), but route() applies bodyCap only through readJson when `input` is declared (app/_server/route.ts:149-156) and this route declares none. Its only bound is the DECLARED content-length (hunt-return/route.ts:35-36); `await req.formData()` at :39 reads any chunked body to the end. Fixed looks like /audio/return/route.ts `cappedForm` (a counting TransformStream that errors past the cap) - or, better, the seam card below.

## Flow
- POST /audio/hunt-return with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a 128 MiB body
- route() skips its cap (no input schema) -> declared = 0 passes the check
- req.formData() buffers 128 MiB, then the parse/door refuses

## Expected impact
The operator's server (Cloud Run instance memory) stops buffering an uncapped upload from any access-holding client. Could break: a client that streams without a length and exceeds 60 MB, which is already over the cap.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the cap the route declares binds a body that declares no length
Before: by analogy with the measured /audio/return (67108864 of 67108864 B pulled); not measured on this route
After: <= cap + 2 chunks pulled, 400 'the upload is over 60 MB'
Method: simulation - the identical code shape was measured in tests/next-server/audio-return.test.ts; this route is in audio-hunt, not this round's scope
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/audio/hunt-return/route.ts:33-39
app/_server/route.ts:149-156 (bodyCap only reaches readJson)
tests/next-server/audio-return.test.ts 'reads a body that declares no length only up to the cap'
instrument: copy the chunked-body case of tests/next-server/audio-return.test.ts against hunt-return's POST; seed red on HEAD, green after

title: route() does not apply bodyCap to a route that declares no input
body:
## Summary
app/_server/route.ts enforces `bodyCap` only inside readJson; 4 routes pass bodyCap > 0 with no `input`, so the option is silently inert for them.

## Description
RouteOptions.bodyCap is documented 'The most body bytes read' (app/_server/route.ts:57), but route() calls readJson(req, opts.bodyCap, ...) only when opts.input is set (:149-151); with no input and bodyCap > 0 the body is handed to the handler unread and uncounted. Routes affected: app/(studio)/audio/return/route.ts (now self-capped, 27aa7ffb), app/(studio)/audio/hunt-return/route.ts (uncapped), app/api/import/route.ts (self-counts), app/api/mcp/route.ts (unverified). Fixed looks like: route() wraps req.body in a counting stream bounded by bodyCap for every HAS_BODY method, so a handler's formData()/arrayBuffer() errors past the cap and the envelope answers body-too-large.

## Flow
- a handler declares bodyCap: N and no input
- route() skips readJson
- the handler's req.formData() reads past N

## Expected impact
One rule at the seam instead of a per-route copy; the two return routes and import can drop their own counters. Could break: a route that relied on reading past its declared cap (none known).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one cap rule for every body a route reads
Before: 1 of 4 no-input bodyCap routes bounded by the stated cap at the seam (0 by route(); import and return count themselves)
After: 4 of 4 bounded by route()
Method: simulation - app/_server is outside this round's scope; counted by grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep: route({ ... bodyCap: [^0] without input: -> audio/hunt-return, audio/return, api/import, api/mcp
app/_server/route.ts:57 (doc) vs :149-156 (only readJson applies it)
instrument: a tests/next-server case: a no-input route({bodyCap: 1024}) whose handler awaits req.arrayBuffer(), fed a chunked 1 MiB body; count bytes pulled (seed red on HEAD route.ts)

title: One actor-of-principal helper for the nine inline spellings
body:
## Summary
`"uid" in who ? who.uid : "operator"` is spelled inline at 9 sites in app/ and lib/, 3 of them in this context.

## Description
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/arrangeActs.ts:303 (actorOf, file-private because a 'use server' module may export only async functions), app/(studio)/audio/_audio/actions.ts:224 and app/(studio)/audio/return/route.ts:79 (`who !== null && "uid" in who`) each derive the operator actor from a Principal; grep counts 9 such sites repo-wide. A change to how a token principal is named in the ledger has to find all 9. Fixed looks like an `actorOf(who)` export in lib/principal.ts and the 9 sites calling it.

## Flow
- grep -rn '"uid" in who ? who.uid : "operator"' app lib -> 9
- add lib/principal.ts actorOf; replace the 9 sites
- typecheck + npm test + vitest

## Expected impact
Every ledger actor is derived by one rule. Could break: nothing if the replacement is mechanical; the type pins the shape.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one derivation of the operator actor
Before: 9 inline sites (3 here)
After: 1 definition, 9 call sites
Method: probe - counted by grep; the definition belongs in lib/principal.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn '"uid" in who ? who.uid : "operator"' --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx app lib | wc -l -> 9
instrument: the grep count (9 -> 0 inline) plus typecheck and the vitest lane green

title: One take-file URL builder for the six template literals
body:
## Summary
The take file URL `/api/sound/takes/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/file` is built by hand at 6 server sites (2 in this context) beside lib/sound/client.ts takeFileUrl, which is client-only.

## Description
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/arrangeRead.ts:62, app/(studio)/audio/_audio/read.ts:83, app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/read.ts:76, app/(studio)/audio/_insight/read.ts:124, lib/library/feeds/sound.ts:80 and lib/decision/v1/sources/audio.ts:219 each spell the route; lib/sound/client.ts:19 is the client spelling (through withAccess, and 'use client'-bound, so the server cannot call it). A move of the file route has six places to miss. Fixed looks like a server-safe `takeFileHref(id)` in lib/sound (pure) used by the six, with client.ts wrapping it.

## Flow
- grep 'api/sound/takes/${encodeURIComponent' -> 6 server + 1 client
- add the pure helper, replace the six
- typecheck + tests

## Expected impact
One spelling of a URL four screens draw. Could break: nothing if mechanical.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one spelling of the take file route
Before: 6 hand-built server sites
After: 1 helper, 6 calls
Method: probe - counted by grep; 4 of the 6 sites are outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn 'api/sound/takes/${encodeURIComponent' app lib packages -> 7 lines (6 server, lib/sound/client.ts:19 client)
instrument: the grep count (6 -> 0 template literals outside the helper) plus typecheck
